llm.reply:
The KRAS gene product is a GTPase belonging to the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The OMIM record for this gene is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. Its molecular activity is that of a signaling switch, and oncogenic mutations lock that switch on [26: "its mutations result in constitutive activation of the KRAS protein, which acts as a molecular switch"].

## GTPase switch function

When mutated, KRAS is constitutively active and continuously drives downstream pathways that support proliferation and survival [26: "its mutations result in constitutive activation of the KRAS protein, which acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. Alternative splicing produces two protein isoforms that differ at the C-terminus [11: "Alternative splicing leads to variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"].

## Activating mutations

A single amino acid substitution is enough to produce an activating mutation [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. The resulting transforming protein is implicated in lung adenocarcinoma, pancreatic ductal carcinoma and colorectal carcinoma [11: "implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"]. In colorectal cancer, oncogenic KRAS activates a downstream transcription factor [28: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2)"].

## Targeting the activity

KRAS was long considered undruggable until G12C-specific inhibitors were developed [26: "KRAS was historically thought to be an undruggable target until the development of KRASG12C allele-specific inhibitors"]. Other mutant forms may be targeted indirectly by inhibiting the exchange factor that activates KRAS [29: "The other KRAS mutations may be targeted indirectly via inhibition of the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"].

llm.reply:
KRAS encodes a small GTPase [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. It works as a molecular switch that, once constitutively activated by mutation, keeps stimulating downstream signaling for proliferation and survival [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. The gene symbol is KRAS [1].

## Gene identity and activation

The gene name is KRAS [5]. The OMIM record is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. The literature entity name is Kras [6]. A single residue change can make the protein constitutively active [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"].

## ClinVar variant records

One ClinVar record is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. Another is NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23].

## Oncogenic signaling and targeting

One review is titled Role of oncogenic KRAS in the prognosis, diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer. [2]. Another is titled KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer. [9]. Another is titled Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression. [14]. Another is titled Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer. [18]. Another is titled Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders. [22].

One linked publication is PMID 34742312 [8]. Another is PMID 34776511 [13]. Another is PMID 37768068 [17]. Another is PMID 38686056 [21]. Another is PMID 39298590 [25].

Direct KRAS targeting has advanced through G12C inhibitors [27: "KRAS (G12C) inhibitors, such as AMG510 (sotorasib) and MRTX849 (adagrasib), which have obtained encouraging results in clinical trials"]. In colorectal cancer, mutant KRAS turns fibroblasts into lipid-rich cells that drive angiogenesis [28: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2) that upregulates the expression of the proadipogenic factors BMP4 and WNT5B"]. KRAS mutations are frequent in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma [29: "mutated in up to 90% of all pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs)"]. A heterobifunctional degrader has been designed against many KRAS alleles [30: "potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"].

## Clinical trials

One trial is Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Another is PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Another is A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. Another is Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. Another is A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
